findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot falls on a day that has a date override, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true inside the `dateOverrides.find()` callback, and the callback returns undefined for slots that are *within* the override window. Control then hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and the function returns immediately, before the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom. Consequence: for any slot covered by a date override, the host's existing bookings and calendar busy times are never consulted, so a host with a date override who already has a conflicting booking (Cal booking or external calendar event) will still be shown as available and can be double-booked. The override check must not short-circuit the busy check.

findings.title: Dayjs object identity comparison `===` is always false, killing the start==end override case
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created Dayjs object references, which are always distinct, so this condition never fires (it is dead code). The intent was to detect overrides where start equals end (Cal.com's representation for an unavailable period). Because the check is dead, a slot that starts exactly at such an override's start time fails all the other conditions (`slotEndTime` is not before the start, `slotStartTime` is not after the end), `find` returns undefined, `dateOverrideExist` is true, and the function returns `true` — marking the slot available when the user explicitly blocked it. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()`.

findings.title: Working-hours check computes `end` identical to `start`, so slot end time is never validated
findings.body: In the new working-hours check inside `checkIfIsAvailable`: `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — `end` is the same expression as `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` only ever compares the slot's *start* minute against the working-hours end. A slot that starts within working hours but ends after them passes the check. `end` should be derived from the slot end (e.g. `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute() + eventLength`, or better from `slotEndTime`), otherwise this availability validation is wrong for any event whose slot would overrun the host's working hours.

findings.title: Date-override day comparison is formatted in the server's local timezone, making results server-TZ dependent
findings.body: The day-match uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is explicitly UTC (`.utc()`), but the left-hand side is a plain Dayjs formatted without `.utc()`/`.tz()`, so it renders in whatever timezone the Node process runs in. On a server whose TZ is not UTC (common in non-UTC deployments), the same override/slot pair can land on different formatted days, so the override either fails to match (override ignored, host shown available on an overridden day) or matches the wrong day. Additionally, only the override's *start* day is compared, so an override window that crosses midnight UTC is only applied to one of the two UTC days it spans. The shifted value should be formatted with `.utc()` to match the right-hand side.

findings.title: `override.timeZone` is used without a fallback although the type declares it optional
findings.body: `const organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset();` assumes `override.timeZone` is always set, but this PR adds `timeZone?: string` to `TimeRange` as optional. Any caller of `getSlots` that supplies date overrides without a timezone (which the type explicitly permits — only the `getSchedule` call site populates it) will have dayjs fall back to the process/browser-local timezone for the offset computation, silently producing wrong override windows. Either make the field required on the `GetSlots` input type or fall back to `organizerTimeZone`.

findings.title: No test for the headline fix: date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin events
findings.body: The PR's primary bug fix (#8207) is that date overrides of *fixed* hosts are enforced for ROUND_ROBIN events (the new `isFixed`-aware filtering plus the date-override/working-hours logic in `checkIfIsAvailable`). The only test added exercises a single-user event's date override in a different invitee timezone; every team-event scenario in the suite uses `hosts: []` and no date overrides, so all round-robin hosts are loose hosts. There is no regression test where a fixed round-robin host has a date override and the slot list must be restricted accordingly — exactly the logic most likely to regress (and where the busy-check bypass above would be caught). Add a test with a ROUND_ROBIN event, one fixed host with a date override, one round-robin host without, asserting only the fixed host's override window is offered.
